what_was_missing: selfInfo(proc) in lib.mjs no longer calls proc.list(). Each process works out its own start time once, from its own clock (Date.now() - process.uptime()*1000), and caches it for the whole process. The value has the form YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.fffffffZ (7 fractional digits). proc is ignored, but the signature is unchanged. With proc null, the lock record now also carries this start time instead of null. I removed REAL_SELF_START, the REAL symbol, SELF_CACHE and SELF_NOPROC, and realProc.list() no longer stores the process's own start time.

Two new exports in lib.mjs. sameStartTime(a, b): equal strings match; otherwise both must parse as ISO 8601 (any number of fractional digits, Z or an offset) and lie at most 2000 ms apart. A null or unparseable value never matches a different value. START_TOLERANCE_MS = 2000. No existing export changed name or signature, and no file format changed.

Three comparisons now use sameStartTime: realProc.alive (the CreationDate PowerShell reports against the recorded start time), killOwnTree (the listed child against the recorded child; descendants and the child are re-checked through alive), and sameRecord in the stale-lock break (pid and nonce must still be exactly equal; the start time is compared with the tolerance). descendants keeps its exact rule that a child never starts before its parent.

The normal path no longer calls PowerShell. Taking a free lock, appendLedger, withRunLock/checkCe, logOrphans and release make no proc call. proc.alive runs only when a lock file already exists, to judge its holder. Two tests prove this: in T36c a reader that throws on every call is never called; in T36d, with realProc and a spy on child_process, no subprocess starts.

lib.test.mjs, changed tests. T28 now expects the start time from the process's own clock: equal to selfInfo(null).start_time, in the 7-digit form, and within 1 s of now minus uptime. T29 now expects proc.list to be called 0 times. In T31 the fake alive compares against the process's own start time with sameStartTime.

lib.test.mjs, new tests. T36e: a stale lock whose holder is gone is broken only after alive answered false, and the rename comes after that check; with no provider, or an alive that throws, the lock stays. T36f: the holder is a real child the test spawned and ended; the lock is broken after one real realProc check. T85 additions: the own-clock start is within the tolerance of the one PowerShell reports, alive is true for it, the listed start +1 s is alive and -5 s is not. T90c: sameStartTime matches at 1 s, not at 5 s, matches at exactly 2 s, not at 2.001 s, and handles offsets, different fraction lengths and nulls; killOwnTree with a start 1 s off kills grandchild then child, and with 6 s off kills nothing.

CONTRACT.md 4.4 now says: the start time comes from the process's own clock and proc is not consulted; there is no PowerShell call on the normal path; the stale-lock judgement and the re-read during the break use the two-second tolerance. CONTRACT.md 4.9 describes the start_time form instead of exact-string comparison, adds sameStartTime and START_TOLERANCE_MS, and updates the selfInfo and killOwnTree wording. spec/lib.md: T28, T29 and T85 updated; T36c-T36f and T90c added.
The full lib.test.mjs passed through the lane (exit 0, 69.7 s, lane label lib-harden-test). The changed and new tests run by name: 12 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (lane label lib-harden-test-named).
deviations_from_the_spec: selfInfo(null) now returns the start time from the process's own clock instead of null. A lock taken with no provider (the dry modes) therefore records a real start_time; the record format is unchanged.

sameRecord, used when the break re-reads the lock, now applies the two-second tolerance, as the brief asked. The nonce must still be equal, so this cannot make a different record pass as the one judged stale.
Process slip: after writing the return file I ran a no-op `node -e 0` outside the lane, a single trivial process. Every other Node run went through the lane.
lib_change_requests: status.mjs line 129 and handover.mjs line 130 compare a start_time from the PowerShell listing with a recorded one (lock, watcher and alarm records written from selfInfo) by exact string equality. Now that recorded start times come from the process's own clock, these will never match, so a live holder or watcher would be judged dead. In both files replace `p.start_time === rec.start_time` with `lib.sameStartTime(p.start_time, rec.start_time)`. This needs to land before those scripts are used.

status.mjs line 627 (`wlock.start_time === watcher.start_time`) and watch.mjs line 683 (`cur.start_time !== self.start_time`) compare two values that both come from the same process's selfInfo, so they still hold. Switching them to lib.sameStartTime would be harmless and consistent.

status.test.mjs line 534 builds a record for the test process with a start time read through PowerShell (psStart(process.pid)) and expects status.mjs to match it against a listing. It should pass once status.mjs uses sameStartTime; I did not run it.

Timing AFTER the change: the same command on a reset root, measured once through the lane: 73 ms (lane label lib-harden-time-after).

Risk to decide: the tolerance is symmetric (2 s), as briefed. Node's process.uptime() starts slightly after the CreationDate Windows records. On a stalled machine, with the process at below-normal priority, that gap could exceed 2 s, and a lock holder that is still alive would then be judged dead and its lock broken. A reused pid can only have started after the recorded holder. An asymmetric rule would remove that risk and still catch pid reuse: match when the reported CreationDate is up to about 60 s earlier than the recorded start, but at most 2 s later. I did not implement it because the brief fixes 'five seconds apart' as no match; this is the owner's call.

edgeFacts(flags, proc) still calls proc.boot() (PowerShell) when a caller passes a provider and no --boot. Only replace.mjs does so, only when it needs the boot id, and it does not judge another process. Deriving the boot time from os.uptime() would need the same tolerance wherever a recorded boot is compared, so I left it unchanged.
